title: The disjointness fooling set
statement: Fix $n \in \bbn$, and consider the set-disjointness function on subsets of $[n]$, namely the Boolean function $g(X, Y)$ that is $\mathtt{true}$ exactly when $X \cap Y = \emptyset$. Then the collection $\{(X, X^c) \mid X \subseteq [n]\}$ of complementary pairs is a fooling set for $g$: for every rectangle $R = A \times B$ (with $A, B$ families of subsets of $[n]$) that is monochromatic for $g$, the intersection of $R$ with this collection contains at most one point.
replaced:
The collection $\{(X, X^c) \mid X \subseteq [n]\}$ is a fooling set for
$\mathrm{disjointness}(n)$: every pair $(X, X^c)$ evaluates to $\mathtt{true}$,
and for any monochromatic rectangle $R$ with $\mathrm{disjointness} = \mathtt{true}$
that contains two distinct fooling-set pairs, those pairs must coincide.
